clue.text: Shipping line runs a small container – DON'T OPEN IT!

blocks.note: P and O (P&O) is a British shipping line, written out in full
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
taken as written
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a box is a container

explanation.surface: A ferry company's freight sailing carries a little crate stamped with a stern warning not to open it.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a long-established British ferry and cruise company; the ampersand is spelt out as AND.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora was told never to open the jar, which released all evils when she did, so the exclamation is a cryptic gloss.

clue.text: Innkeepers up from the south served up one pound tins

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards turns the word round
served up in a down light means presented upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one; LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
tins and cans are the same thing

explanation.surface: Landlords bring cans of something up from the cellar for a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate reversals: the word up itself is read upwards, then one pound is read upwards before tins is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican is the licensee who runs a pub, the modern equivalent of an innkeeper.

clue.text: Rotating neon "Go" sign that's seen on the road

definitions.text: sign that's seen on the road

indicators.note: something rotated half a turn ends up facing the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A spinning neon sign reading Go stands by the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: NEON reads the same letters backwards as NOEN, which supplies the first two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-entry sign is a familiar road sign forbidding vehicles from going in.

clue.text: Torches trained around those stuck in pit

indicators.note: the answer lies around inside the run of words, spread across the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word into the second word

explanation.surface: Torch beams are pointed at miners trapped down a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The pit is not a mine but the orchestra pit below the front of a theatre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre musicians play in the sunken orchestra pit, so they are the people confined there during a show.

clue.text: Adult Hardy girl put up cash, for example

indicators.note: in a down light, putting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: A is the film classification for adult
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A grown-up daughter of the Hardy family stumps up some money.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is one example of an asset, an item of value owned by a person or business.

clue.text: Rest – have a dip outside walls in Rome

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its boundaries, so only its outside letters are kept
one piece sits outside the other, wrapping round it

blocks.note: to bathe is to take a swim or dip
the first and last letters of the city name

explanation.surface: Holiday advice for Rome: relax and take a swim outside the old city walls.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe can mean to pause and rest, as in letting someone breathe for a moment.

clue.text: Social network switching over one new element

indicators.note: switching something over flips it end to end, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: X is the social network formerly called Twitter
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone moves over to a fresh social media platform.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a chemical element, one of the noble gases used in lamps.

clue.text: Moral story following murder victim with a twist at the end

indicators.text: with a twist at the end
indicators.note: twisting the tail of a word swaps round its closing letters

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
Abel was murdered by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: A cautionary tale about a murder whose ending has a surprise twist.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters of the brother's name trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short tale, often with animal characters, that teaches a moral lesson.

clue.text: Asians, if hot, changing one into cool clothing

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Some people from Asia, feeling the heat, switch into lighter outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes cool mean less warm; in the definition it means stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashionista is a devotee of the latest trends, someone keen on stylish dress.

clue.text: Aunt chews exotic snack item

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar form

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An aunt munches on some foreign nibble.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashews are kidney-shaped nuts commonly eaten salted as a snack.

clue.text: T-bone chop he cooked – IT's not for her

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters are worked into new order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: He grills steak and chops, but that is not to her taste.
explanation.walkthrough: IT means information technology, not the pronoun it.
explanation.definitionFit: A technophobe fears or dislikes technology, so computing and IT hold no appeal for such a person.

clue.text: One standing in alley likely to get knocked over?

definitions.text: One standing in alley likely to get knocked over?

blocks.clueFragment: One standing in alley likely to get knocked over?
blocks.note: surface reading: a person loitering in a back street who is likely to be mugged

blocks.clueFragment: One standing in alley likely to get knocked over?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a pin set up at the end of a bowling alley waiting to be bowled down

explanation.walkthrough: The alley is a skittle alley, the lane in the old pub game of skittles, a forerunner of ten-pin bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles are upright wooden pins set at the end of an alley for players to topple with a ball.

clue.text: Enormous disaster brought to us by Cameron?

definitions.text: disaster brought to us by Cameron?

blocks.note: first meaning: gigantic, of huge size

blocks.clueFragment: disaster brought to us by Cameron?
blocks.note: second meaning: the 1912 liner sinking, filmed by James Cameron in 1997

explanation.walkthrough: Cameron tempts British solvers towards the former prime minister David Cameron; it is the film director James Cameron.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for gigantic and also the name of the doomed ship that Cameron's blockbuster film portrayed.

clue.text: Country relations advanced 50 yen

blocks.note: IT is a coy crossword term for sexual relations
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
L is the Roman numeral for 50
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Diplomatic ties between nations helped by a loan of fifty yen.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a European nation, so a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Actor for Macbeth? For starters try ringing old McKellen maybe

indicators.note: starters are the opening courses, so only the opening letters of the next words are taken

blocks.note: the initial letters of these two words
aged means old
Sir Ian McKellen is the British stage and screen actor

explanation.surface: A casting director suggests phoning veteran Ian McKellen to play the Scottish king.
explanation.walkthrough: McKellen, a famous Macbeth, sits in the surface as the obvious candidate, but only his first name is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is a tragedy, so the lead role calls for a tragedian, an actor who specialises in tragic parts.

clue.text: Foreshadow a speechless judge

blocks.note: taken as written
dumb means unable to speak
to rate something is to assess or judge it

explanation.surface: A judge is struck silent, foreseeing what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to give a faint outline of something in advance, which is to hint at or prefigure it.

clue.text: Reportedly, the compiler defames resident of northern island

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or told, so we go by speech rather than spelling

blocks.note: the compiler refers to himself as I; slander means to defame

explanation.surface: Word has it that the setter has been bad-mouthing someone who lives in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves the compiler or this setter, standing for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander is a native or inhabitant of Iceland, a large island in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Back in Beirut, a ref's only having a horror show

indicators.note: the answer is sitting in the run of words that follows
going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are taken right to left

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the city name to the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A football referee in Beirut finds himself in a nightmare match.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosferatu is the 1922 German silent vampire film, a classic of horror cinema.

clue.text: Journey fuelled by self-confidence?

blocks.note: surface reading: an actual voyage undertaken on the strength of self-belief
setter's reading: an activity pursued chiefly to flatter one's own vanity

explanation.walkthrough: The journey is only figurative; the phrase means indulging one's sense of importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an undertaking done for self-gratification, literally a trip powered by one's own sense of self.

clue.text: Meryl has no right, dear

indicators.note: having none of something means it is missing, so that letter is dropped from the name

blocks.note: Meryl Streep is the American film actress
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Meryl is told she has no right to something, my dear.
explanation.walkthrough: Dear here means expensive, not a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep describes a price that is excessively high, just as dear can mean costly.

clue.text: Raised Ms Batty's clothing – fine, feminine, orange-yellow coloured

indicators.note: in a down light, raising something lifts it so the letters read from bottom to top
clothing covers what is inside it, so one part wraps around the other

blocks.note: Nora Batty is the stocking-wearing character in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine; keep the possessive S
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
F is the abbreviation for feminine

explanation.surface: Nora Batty hitches up her outfit, which is fine, feminine and bright orange.
explanation.walkthrough: Last of the Summer Wine was a long-running BBC comedy about pensioners in Yorkshire; Nora Batty is famous for her wrinkled stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron, from the crocus spice, names the deep orange-yellow shade the spice gives food.

clue.text: A twit so daft got the job done

indicators.note: daft means silly or crazy, suggesting the letters have gone haywire

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Even a foolish twit managed to finish the task.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to it is an idiom for taking care of a task, so the past form means made sure it was done.

clue.text: Loud cry beginning to wind bear up

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
in a down light, up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's famous bear

explanation.surface: The start of a gusty wind stirs up a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud shout of excitement or joy.

clue.text: Subject closed, constable placing one under arrest

indicators.note: arresting someone means taking them into custody, so the officer holds a piece inside

blocks.note: a door pushed to is shut
PC is the abbreviation for police constable
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A case is shut once a police officer arrests a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject matter under discussion.

clue.text: Fit-looking ball-boy regularly knocked out beefy individual?

indicators.note: knocking out every other letter at a steady interval leaves only the alternate ones

blocks.note: buff is slang for physically fit and muscular
the second, fourth and sixth letters survive

explanation.surface: A muscular ball boy at a tennis match is knocked unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefy is the pun: a buffalo is a large bovine animal, so a source of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffalo is a heavy wild ox, a cattle-like beast, so jokingly a beefy creature.

clue.text: Make new approach when acquiring the ultimate in holy books

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so these letters are reshaped
the ultimate is the last, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A religious scholar rethinks their approach to the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical books of disputed authority, printed in some Bibles but excluded from others.

clue.text: Diarist Jones stripped off long narrow top

indicators.note: stripping something removes its outer layer, so the end letters of the name come away

blocks.note: Bridget Jones is the diary-keeping heroine of Helen Fielding's novels

explanation.surface: The diarist Jones takes off a long skimpy top.
explanation.walkthrough: Top is a mountain crest, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow raised strip of land, such as the crest along a hill or mountain range.

clue.text: One helping the flow when Holmes has a tricky problem?

definitions.text: One helping the flow when Holmes has a tricky problem?

blocks.clueFragment: One helping the flow when Holmes has a tricky problem?
blocks.note: surface reading: an assistant who keeps the detective's thinking moving on a hard case

blocks.clueFragment: One helping the flow when Holmes has a tricky problem?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a bristly wire that clears blockages so smoke draws freely through a smoker's stem

explanation.walkthrough: Holmes called a hard case a three-pipe problem, smoking as he thought, so his pipe would need clearing afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fluffy wire tool pushed through a tobacco pipe's stem to clear tar and keep the airflow free.
